lessons.subject: writing
lessons.lesson_title: Finish and Revise: Evidence and Reasoning
lessons.previous_learning: Day 15 preparation work was completed, but the required 7-9 sentence analytical paragraph about Nadia's stronger final explanation was left unfinished.
lessons.course_context: Finish yesterday's incomplete analytical response before adding new writing demands.
learning_objectives: Use two exact details from the text.
Revise for vague wording and sentence boundaries.
lessons.why_it_matters: Finishing and revising are part of writing, not optional steps after the real assignment.

vocabulary.definition: the exact thing that happened or was said
why the detail helps prove your claim
making writing clearer or stronger after the first draft

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: yesterday's paragraph was not finished. Today you finish it first, then revise it. Use this simple order: CLAIM -> EVIDENCE 1 -> WHY IT MATTERS -> EVIDENCE 2 -> WHY IT MATTERS -> CONCLUSION.

worked_examples.title: Evidence plus reasoning
worked_examples.problem: Why is Nadia's final explanation stronger?
worked_examples.solution: The lights fail again seven seconds after the balcony spots are turned back on. That repeated timing gives her a reason to include the electrical load instead of blaming only the old cable.
worked_examples.explanation: The reasoning says what the evidence proves.

independent_practice.prompt: Write 7-9 sentences: Why is Nadia's final explanation stronger than her first one? Use TWO exact details. After each detail, explain why it matters. End with a conclusion.

exit_ticket.prompt: Complete the revision check: 7-9 sentences, two exact details, reasoning after each, one vague word replaced, punctuation checked, conclusion adds something new.
exit_ticket.answer: A complete revised paragraph meeting all six checklist items.

lessons.voice_prompt: Speak directly to Atticus. Keep directions short. Do not dictate sentences. If he gives evidence without reasoning, ask: What does that detail prove? If he is stuck on a word, define it quickly. Do not let the session end with the paragraph unfinished.
lessons.teacher_notes: Completion is the main writing habit target today.
